videos.title: The Science of Learning Math (and Anything Else) with Justin Skycak
videos.description: I got the chance to interview the learning legend Justin Sky-zack on a whole lot of topics around learning technical stuff like math efficiently.   He applied these techniques to building ai-driven system for math academy where he is currently the Chief Quant, Director of Analytics.  we’re going to cover:  - His learning backstory.  - What cognitive science says about the fastest path to mastery.  - And his practical advice for adults, kids, old people, people with ADHD, researchers.  Important Links: 📌 Justin's personal website: https://www.justinmath.com/ 📌 Justin on X: https://x.com/justinskycak 📌 Justin's math journey: https://www.justinmath.com/bio/ 📌 Math Academy: https://mathacademy.com/  📌 also btw if you want learn to code from full-stack to AI with Scrimba https://scrimba.com/?via=yacineMahdid  (extra 20% off pro with my link, great resource, I love the team)  Table of Content: - intro: 0:00 - justin skycak background : 2:10 - 3000h math self study in high school: 5:45 - what a day looked like for that 3000h stretch: 11:45 - meta-learning vs pure math learning: 16:10 - when did you get into cognitive neuro?: 21:50 - how did the fundamental math helped in your research projects: 29:55 - what does the math academy learning system looks like: 43:10 - how did you guys build the 2000 topic knowledge graph: 47:34 - would LLM be useful as an interface to that knowledge graph for the students?: 1:01:15 - how does the FIRe spaced repetition algorithm works?: 1:10:46 - does the same knowledge graph structure would work for physics? or other topic?: 1:17:34 - how do you understand the subject vs the curiculum: 1:34:05 - is there a connection between studying math and learning a sport?: 1:35:50 - do you think in math doing and teaching requires different skills?: 1:42:00 - could you get understanding without automaticy?1:56:25 - do you see any upside of confusion in learning?: 2:05:35 - learning math as an adult?: 2:14:11 - how to fill the motivation gap after learning the fundamental?: 2:19:20 - how should teaching math for kids and adults balance fundamentals and creativity?: 2:24:10 - is it ever too late to learn math seriously?: 2:33:55 - mastery learning vs ultra learning: 2:46:00 - top-down vs bottom-up: 2:51:30 - mastery learning for domain without a structured hierarchical structure? 2:53:40 - neurodivergence / adhd for structured math learning?: 2:56:30 - amateur mathematician augmented with technology will be able to contribute to research?: 3:06:20 - what are you most excited about right now in term of learning: 3:14:37 - conclusion: 3:17:12  Also other links about math academy: 📌 Fractional Implicit Repetition (FIRe): https://www.justinmath.com/individualized-spaced-repetition-in-hierarchical-knowledge-structures/   📌 The Math Academy Way: https://www.justinmath.com/files/the-math-academy-way.pdf Math Academy's working draft book, authored by Justin, which answers the following questions: - What techniques exist to maximize student learning and talent development, particularly in the context of math?  - Why are these techniques so impactful, and if they are indeed so impactful, then why are they so often absent from traditional classrooms?  - How does Math Academy leverage these techniques?  And some of the other people's stories that we’re discussed 📌 Melbourne's journey from "not a math person" to deriving batchnorm and building robot dynamics from scratch: https://melbournebaldove.com/logs/math-academy-journey  📌 Sayid's story about overcoming his math anxiety - https://x.com/sayidislearning/status/1884326740417470527  "Around the 60 day mark my brain was like ... "we thought this was a temporary thing, but it doesn't seem like you're going to stop doing this any time soon, so we're going to have to do some rewiring to make sure you're not feeling repulsed, you're not feeling anxious." And then magically one day these feelings just completely went away. ... When I was starting out learning math I wasn't really sure if that feeling of waking up and not looking forward to starting my day with math was ever going to go away. But I'm pretty sure that if you stick with something long enough, then it will just become the new normal for you. Your brain, your body will eventually be forced to adjust."  Additional more learning materials  📌 Introduction to Algorithms and Machine Learning: https://www.justinmath.com/files/introduction-to-algorithms-and-machine-learning.pdf   textbook Justin wrote while teaching the most advanced math/CS sequence in the USA, scaffolding high school students up to doing masters/PhD-level coursework: reproducing academic research papers in artificial intelligence, building everything from scratch in Python.  ---- Follow Me Online Here: Twitter: https://twitter.com/yacinelearning LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/yacinemahdid/ ___  Have a great week! 👋

videos.title: LLM Ops Foundation: Building & Scaling Generative AI Systems in Production
videos.description: In this video, we dive deep into the foundations of LLM Ops (Large Language Model Operations). While MLOps revolutionized how we handle structured data and predictive models, LLMs introduce a new set of challenges from non-deterministic outputs to the complexities of prompt engineering and high inference costs.  What you will learn in this session: 1. The Definition of LLM Ops: Why it’s more than just a naming trend. 2. MLOps vs. LLM Ops: Understanding the shift from operationalizing "models" to operationalizing "systems." 3. The 4 Key Characteristics of LLMs: Free-form text, non-determinism, prompt dependency, and economic management. 4. New Operational Responsibilities: A look at prompt versioning, retrieval pipelines (RAG), safety guardrails, and cost control.  Whether you are a Data Scientist, DevOps Engineer, or AI Enthusiast, this video will give you the mindset shift needed to move Generative AI from a notebook into a reliable production environment.

videos.title: Gemini 3: The Multimodal AI That's Reshaping Development
videos.description: Gemini 3 is not just answering prompts anymore. It is planning, building, and verifying real software.  This session breaks down what makes Gemini 3 different, then walks through practical demos that show generative UI, agentic development, and multimodal reasoning in action. Expect a clear look at how Gemini 3 Pro is used inside Canvas and how agent-driven tools can take a high-level goal and turn it into working code.  This is built for US learners exploring AI for software development, product prototyping, and workflow automation, especially anyone trying to move faster than traditional “code everything by hand” cycles. It also helps teams evaluate where multimodal AI fits, how to prompt for multi-step builds, and what to look for when trusting AI-generated output.  Key concepts covered include Gemini 3 speed and reasoning, what the HLE (Humanity’s Last Exam) benchmark is and why it matters, choosing the right model (3 Pro) and tools (Deep Research, Create Videos, Create Images, Canvas, Guided Learning), building a Paris travel planner React app from a single prompt, turning a 2D floor plan into an interactive 3D viewer and upgrading it with a walkthrough recorder, understanding Antigravity as an agented IDE built on Code OSS, using planning mode plus artifacts for trust and verification, and replicating a dashboard layout from a video into React and Tailwind CSS. videos.title: OpenAI’s Genius Plan Can’t Possibly Fail
videos.description: OpenAI has a plan to cure cancer! It’s … not very good.   Learn more by reading “How AI Can, and Can't, Cure Cancer” at https://curecancer.ai/   You can support me on Patreon at https://www.patreon.com/Siliconversations   Special thanks to my Patreon supporters:  Sentient Hat Tier: Maple the Finn Nathanaël Havez MyDailyPintOfGremlinMilk Matias Badino Tom your personal annoying Bug Kelly P Old_leginary (hun vaze) C_Bookie Alexandre Le Mercier  Big Sentient Hat Tier: darkprincedarkstar  Emmanuel Goldstein Red Ransil Aaron Smith Sirhaian  Julian Schulz Dawid Kubicki Harrier 🦊 Snababo Jacob Mejer botfly Borderlands2 screaming gun Call Your Reps About AI Safety Patrick Kennedy Drew Spartz Sarunas Budreckis Linkie Pup raided Drarko Bread Shark Sayhan Yalvaçer Jeffrey  qqlululu  MrConchman Sequoia michael fares David  Siliconversations is financially supported by the Future of Life Institute. Go to https://futureoflife.org/ to learn more.   All my opinions are my own.  This video was: Written, directed and narrated by Siliconversations Illustrated and edited by Maris Tockler  Sources:  How AI Can, and Can't, Cure Cancer https://curecancer.ai/   Looking Glass Universe: The Embarrassingly Simple Reason AI Can't Cure Cancer -  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zFcyWFK1q8I  Nature News: AI linked to explosion of low-quality biomedical research papers - https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-01592-0   Claim: There are approx. 37 trillion cells in the human body  Source: Annals of Human Biology: An estimation of the number of cells in the human body - https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.3109/03014460.2013.807878   Claim: There are approx. 7 billion billion billion atoms in the human body  Source: The Wikipedia article “Composition of the human body” https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_of_the_human_body says that there are 7 octillion (billion billion billion) atoms in the human body, citing this blog as their source: https://web.archive.org/web/20250207160554/https://education.jlab.org/qa/mathatom_04.html  I was suspicious of this source because it claimed that 99% of the body's mass is composed of Hydrogen, Oxygen and Carbon, while the Wikipedia article shows a diagram claiming that the body is 3% Nitrogen. https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/201_Elements_of_the_Human_Body.02.svg/500px-201_Elements_of_the_Human_Body.02.svg.png  I don’t know which of these claims is correct, and I didn’t want to go down a whole research rabbit hole about it. Fortunately, the Wikipedia article also provides a table that shows estimates of the mass and atomic percent of each atom in a 69 kg body, sourced from the book:  Emsley J (25 August 2011). Nature's Building Blocks: An A-Z Guide to the Elements. OUP Oxford. p. 83. ISBN 978-0-19-960563-7. Retrieved 17 June 2016. I did some quick maths using the table, and based on the values provided for Oxygen, Carbon and Hydrogen, I estimated that a 69kg human body has 6.5, 6.87 and 6.65 Octillion atoms, respectively. Some people weigh more than 69kg, so 7 Octillion is a good enough estimate for the throwaway claim I made in this YouTube video.   AI Use Disclosure: YouTube generated the subtitles, which I partially formatted using Claude.
